input_oneliner: 54M metastatic prostate CA admitted for pain control, overnight says legs heavy, trouble standing, mid-back pain worse

reference_targets_freetext.item: Sensory level to pinprick and temperature on the trunk, and vibration sense in the legs
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: A sensory level localizes cord compression and is the single most useful bedside finding for a myelopathy

reference_targets_freetext.item: Deep tendon reflexes in the legs, plantar responses (Babinski), and tone
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Hyperreflexia and extensor plantars indicate cord compression; areflexia points to GBS or cauda equina

reference_targets_freetext.item: Saddle sensation, digital rectal examination (DRE) - anal tone, and bladder percussion/palpation for retention
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Saddle anesthesia, reduced anal tone, and painless retention are the red flags for cauda equina and lower cord involvement

reference_targets_freetext.item: Spinal percussion tenderness and ask whether pain is worse lying flat or at night
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Localizes the vertebral level of metastatic involvement

reference_targets_freetext.item: Ask: onset and progression, bowel or bladder change, and whether weakness is symmetric; test hip flexion strength and sit-to-stand
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Defines pattern and speed of progression; bilateral symmetric leg weakness with back pain in cancer is cord compression until proven otherwise

reference_targets_freetext.item: Medication review (MAR): steroid, opioid, and diuretic dose changes
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Steroid myopathy and hypokalemia are treatable confounders in this population

off_bedside_acceptable: Dexamethasone and spine/oncology consult once compression suspected
should_not_recommend: Increasing opioids for back pain before a neurologic exam
Plain spine films as a substitute for neurologic examination
Waiting for a morning MRI slot before examining for a sensory level and retention

perturbation_pair.changed_feature: comorbidity: metastatic prostate cancer -> Campylobacter gastroenteritis 2 weeks ago
perturbation_pair.input_oneliner: 54M with Campylobacter gastroenteritis 2 weeks ago, admitted for dehydration, overnight says legs heavy, trouble standing, mid-back pain worse
perturbation_pair.expected_change: GBS becomes the leading differential; reflexes (areflexia) remain must-have; single breath count or forced vital capacity for respiratory muscle strength and ask about ascending pattern and paresthesias become must-have; sensory level and spinal percussion tenderness drop to should-still-include.
